messages.subject: 2-Species Occcupancy Model
parts:
To All,

I am attempting to run a two-species interaction model (Richmond et al. 2010) in JAGs. In this model, there is an interaction between the dominant and subordinate species. Also, occupancy of species A & B are modeling as a function of drainage area (these are small stream fish). I'm also assuming that species A does not interfere with the detection of species B; hence the observation processes are structured according to the format of a multi-species model. However, when running the model, I receive the following error, "compilation error on line 10, index is out of range, taking a subset of n". Based on what I've read, my understanding is that this error is being generated because the described dimensionality of the model parameters, does not match the dimensionality of the actual data. If this is an incorrect interpretation, please let me know. I've tried to determine the error, but I keep coming up empty handed. Any help would be much appreciated! Code is below, and data is attached. 

Thanks,

Josh


###Bayesian Hierarchical Models using JAGS (Single-Season Occupany Models)
##MUST DOWNLOAD JAGS for this to work!
#Model Set for All Rivers
data<-read.csv("GD_RD_usfs.csv", header = T, row.names = "Site")

#Subset data by National Forests
HSNF_dat<- subset(data, data$Forest == "Holly Springs")

#Convert intergers > 0 to 1
HSNF_occ<-ifelse(HSNF_dat[,1:8]>0,1,0)

# Separate the two detection histories
DHA <- as.matrix(HSNF_occ[, 1:4])
DHB <- as.matrix(HSNF_occ[, 5:8])

#Aggregate detection data
yA <- rowSums(DHA)
yB <- rowSums(DHB)

nSites <- nrow(HSNF_dat)
zA <- ifelse(yA > 0, 1, NA)
zB <- ifelse(yB > 0, 1, NA)

#Site Covariates
library(robustHD)
DA<- as.numeric(standardize(HSNF_dat$DA))

#observation covariates
Depth_obs<- standardize(HSNF_dat[,22:25])
Velocity_obs<- standardize(HSNF_dat[,26:29])
Substrate_obs<- standardize(HSNF_dat[,30:33])

##2 Species Model With Interaction and Site Covariate
#data 
jagsData <- list(yA = yA, yB = yB, n = 4, nSites = nSites,
                 zA = zA, zB = zB, Depth = Depth_obs, Velocity = Velocity_obs, 
                 Substrate = Substrate_obs, DA = DA)

#Model
require(jagsUI)
#Model
sink("2sps_Int.txt")
cat("model{
  # Likelihood
  for(i in 1:nSites) {
     # Ecological model
     logit(psiA[i]) <- A0 + aDA * DA[i]
     logit(psiB[i]) <- B0 + bDA * DA[i]
     zA[i] ~ dbern(psiA[i])
     zB[i] ~ dbern(psiB[zA[i] + 1])
     # Observation model
     for(j in 1:n[i]) {
      logit(pA[i, j]) <- a0 + aDepth * Depth[i, j] + aVelocity * Velocity[i, j] + 
      aSubstrate * Substrate[i, j]
      logit(pB[i, j]) <- b0 + bDepth * Depth[i, j] + bVelocity * Velocity[i, j] + 
      bSubstrate * Substrate[i, j]
      YA[i, j] ~ dbern(pA[i, j] * zA[i])
      YA[i, j] ~ dbern(pB[i, j] * zB[i])
     }
  }

  # Priors
  # Priors
  pA ~ dbeta(1, 1) # Uninformative priors
  pB ~ dbeta(1, 1)
  psiA ~ dbeta(1, 1)
  psiB[1] ~ dbeta(1, 1)
  psiB[2] ~ dbeta(1, 1)
  A0 ~ dunif(-5, 5)
  B0 ~ dunif(-5, 5)
  a0 ~ dunif(-5, 5)
  b0 ~ dunif(-5,5)
  aDA ~ dunif(-5, 5)
  bDA ~ dunif(-5,5)
  aDepth ~dunif(-5,5)
  bDepth ~ dunif(-5,5)
  aVelocity ~dunif(-5,5)
  bVelocity ~ dunif(-5,5)
  aSubstrate ~dunif(-5,5)
  bSubstrate ~ dunif(-5,5)
}
",fill=TRUE)
sink()

#Parameters Estimated
wanted <- c("pA", "pB", "psiB", "a0", "A0", "b0", "B0", "aDA", "aDepth", 
            "bDepth", "aVelocity", "bVelocity", "aSubstrate", "bSubstrate")

#Run Model
out1 <- jags(jagsData, NULL, wanted, model="2sps_Int.txt",
             n.chains=3, n.burnin = 5000, n.adapt=1000, n.iter=10000,
             parallel=TRUE)

Hi Josh,

Looks like your j loop is referencing n[i] but your jags data object has defined n = 4.  You either need to specify n as a vector of observations for each site (such that length(n) = nSites) or simply remove the i indexing if all sites had 4 observations.
